prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: I keep B009 as my preferred configuration after the full first-round exchange, but with a clearer view of what I am and am not claiming. The test I apply is the original experiment, verified, by the people who did it. In this case the chain is short and documented: Bistritzer and MacDonald published the continuum calculation of flat bands at a magic angle in 2011, and the Jarillo-Herrero group in 2018 showed, in devices tuned only by twist angle and gate voltage, correlated insulating states and superconducting domes. Many independent groups have since reproduced the correlated phases with transport, scanning tunnelling and local-probe measurements, and the platform has opened to other moire systems. That is a door opened to something people could not previously see or tune. I considered moving to B006, which the chair reports as the plurality, and I treat it seriously because it is mature and reproduced. I did not move, because the objection I hear most often against B006, that it follows the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-trap prize, is one I cannot dismiss from my own seat, and because the committee has not yet seen an expert check of the 2001-03 magic-wavelength priority record. I would rather keep a candidate whose priority chain I can state than defer to a vote count. The citation I propose names the prediction and the observed phenomena and makes no claim about the pairing mechanism.
statement.case_against: Three weaknesses remain real. First, the field is about eight years old and the superconducting mechanism is open, which Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll and Pearce each count as a maturity problem; waiting might show which moire results are the lasting core. Second, the 2018 experiments were carried by a group, and Yuan Cao, first author of the two Nature papers, cannot be named within the three-person limit, nor can other experimentalists or earlier theorists of twisted bilayers (Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto; Suarez Morell; Kaxiras and Santos). Third, sample-to-sample variation from twist-angle disorder and strain, which Kroll raises and which I know from the microscopy side, means quantitative phase diagrams are not yet uniformly reproducible. B006 is the more settled prize on every one of these points, and if the committee judges maturity to be decisive it is the defensible outcome.

responses.point: Eriksson argues that B004 is better established because the HgTe quantisation has been confirmed by independent groups across several material families for more than fifteen years, and asks whether Dean, Young and Yacoby are as indispensable as Jarillo-Herrero.
responses.response: I accept the difference in maturity and I have kept B004 as an alternative for that reason. I do not accept that it settles the credit question. The credit boundary for B004 still has to explain why a prediction of the HgTe route by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang stands outside a prize for the experiment that tested it, and the 2016 prize on topological phases is close enough that I would want an expert report on overlap before ranking it first. On the experimental names for B009, Dean, Young and Yacoby contributed important later work on moire heterostructures, but the 2018 discovery that showed correlated insulators and superconductivity at the predicted angle came from the Jarillo-Herrero group. I would keep one experimentalist beside the two theorists and name the junior contributors in the background material, not the citation. I would not support dropping Bistritzer to make room, as I argued in round 1.

responses.point: Kroll says the correlated phases exist but sample variation, twist-angle disorder and strain make the phase diagram hard to reproduce quantitatively, and asks how the experimental credit can be defended when the 2018 first author is not credited.
responses.response: The disorder point is fair and I see it every time I look at such devices: the twist angle varies across a sample, so quantitative comparison between laboratories is hard. My answer is that the qualitative observations have been reproduced across many groups and techniques, which is the standard I apply for verification, and the citation should therefore state only the phenomena. On Yuan Cao, I agree it is an uncomfortable omission and I do not hide it. The prize rule limits us to three people, and the committee has always had to name the leader of the experiment while leaving out the junior first author, as we also would for the HgTe or IceCube experiments. I would put that clearly in the committee's report. I also return Kroll's question about B006 to this table: if the clock case rests on the idea and its realisation, I would ask Kroll who held the magic-wavelength priority, because the 2001-03 record is not something I have checked.

responses.point: Pearce, who prefers B006, says he is unwilling to lead with B012 because only three members ranked it, Knut Urban is missing from the credited names and Chemistry is a plausible home, and he would rather revisit B009 in a few years than reward it now.
responses.response: I agree with Pearce's reading of B012 and I want it on the record that it is not my configuration. It is in my own field, I would step back from it, and the omission of Urban and the Chemistry question are good reasons not to lead with it. On B009 I disagree about waiting. Waiting is costly when the original people are credited by name today and the phenomenon has been reproduced independently. Waiting also invites the usual pressure from later and more beautiful experiments, which is exactly what the prize should not reward. I accept his point that the pairing mechanism is open and that is why I would word the citation around observed states. I also note that Pearce himself moved to B006 mainly after reading the openings, so I would ask him whether the objection that B006 follows the 2005 and 2012 prizes has been answered for him or only outvoted.

responses.point: Johansson prefers B006 because the magic-wavelength idea is a single clear insight reproduced at JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB and SYRTE, and counts the unresolved superconducting pairing in B009 as a maturity concern.
responses.response: I agree that B006 has the cleaner reproduction record and a two-name credit that fits within the limit, and I could support it. Where I differ is in what counts as discovery under our rules. The reproduction across laboratories of an inherited performance level reassures me on verification, but my test also asks who did the original work, and Johansson himself says the 10^-18 milestone belongs to several groups and that the weighting of Katori's concept against Ye's performance record is unsettled. For B009 I accept the mechanism is open, but the existence of the correlated insulators and the gate-tunable superconductivity, which is what the citation would claim, does not depend on it. I would ask Johansson to say what experimental result he would accept as sufficient maturity in B009, so that this is not a judgement of age alone.

responses.point: Danielsson, who prefers B043, has softened on B006 but says no new phenomenon has yet appeared in the clock comparisons, and that the Nobel tradition does not wait for a field to answer every question.
responses.response: I agree with his principle that the tradition does not wait for every question to be answered, and I apply it to B009 in the same way: the superconducting mechanism being open should not by itself block the phenomenon. His remark that clocks have not yet produced a new phenomenon is the same discovery-versus-invention question I put to myself, and it is part of why I keep B009 above B006. On B043 I still cannot be absolutely sure which two names are decisive among AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND, so I would need the outside report he asks for before I could rank it first, even though I agree the diffuse flux is firmly established.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards eight years and an open pairing mechanism as too early; I weigh it less than Eriksson, Kroll and Pearce, but I could be wrong.
Whether a citation can honour both prediction and discovery without implying a mechanism, and whether keeping Bistritzer beside MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero is the best use of the three places.
The 2001-03 priority record for B006 has not been checked by me or, as far as the exchange shows, by anyone; an expert report could make B006 the clearer prize for me.
My recollection of the 2011 to 2018 chain, including the earlier twisted-bilayer theory and the role of Yuan Cao and the experimental co-authors, has not been verified against the primary papers.
I do not know whether a second part could be added to a B009 prize without breaking the three-person limit; on the names currently proposed it cannot.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged in substance. I have no direct tie to the B009 candidates. I am a transmission electron microscopist, so B012 (aberration correction) is in my own field and I would step back from that ballot and not argue for it, which is why it is neither in my configuration nor among my alternatives. Our committee colleague Goran Johansson is also at Chalmers Physics and Bernhard Mehlig is in the neighbouring Gothenburg department, which are departmental links and not conflicts for B009, B006 or B004. I have no relationship with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. I consider no further recusal necessary for myself, and I agree that questions about Kroll, Lindroth and Johansson should be settled by the committee as a whole.
